svg.text: Measure U: the same $300M bond, two rates per $100k
Three $100M tranches (2027, 2032, 2037), each repaid over 30 years at the 5.4% the City's $610M total debt service implies. Same dollars in every
panel; only the base they are divided by changes.
A · What is owed each year — debt service, $M
40-year average $15.2M/yr
— the City's figure
all three tranches, 20 years: $20.3M/yr
tranche 1 · issued 2027
tranche 2 · issued 2032
tranche 3 · issued 2037
hatched = interest
Interest is $310M of the $610M total. Each tranche is a level-payment loan: the payment is the same every year, but in its early years it is mostly
interest and only later mostly principal — that is the time value of money in the picture.
B · What it is divided by — assessed-value base, $B
held at today's base: $30.5B, every year
base the City's rates imply: +4.2%/yr → $160B by 2066
the wedge: base that does not exist yet —
future sales reassessed to market, plus new
construction. It carries 54% of the debt
service.
C · The result — rate per $100k of assessed value (= A ÷ B)
on today's base: $67 for 20 years · $50 average
on the growing base: $23 average ≈ the City's $22.14.
(Steady 4.2%/yr growth peaks at $42 in 2037; the City's own
schedule, growing faster early, says $35 in 2040-41.)
Reading down: the dollars owed (A) are fixed by the bond. The City's advertised $22.14 comes from dividing them by a base (B) that its own rate
schedule assumes will grow about 4.2% a year — that is, from future buyers reassessed at their purchase price and from new buildings. Held on today's
base, the same obligation is $50 on average and $67 for the 20 plateau years. Both are the same $610M; they differ in who pays it.
Source: data/baselines/measure_u_reconciliation_baseline_2026-08-21.json; official figures from Resolution 72,338-N.S. Exhibit B + impartial analysis; base =
Alameda County assessor, Berkeley parcels. Generated by scripts/viz/bond_tranches_svg.py — every number is derived, none typed in.
